text:
Morgan: Hey team — first week new-hire question. I need kubectl access for dev and staging, plus a namespace called `redwood-dev-morgan`. I want to avoid accidentally getting prod creds in my kubeconfig. Also I need to port-forward a local service for debugging. What’s the recommended flow (short-lived kubeconfigs, service account, RBAC, who signs off)?

Jamie (DevEx): Welcome Morgan! :tada: Our usual pattern is: 1) request namespace + port-forward RBAC via the access form, 2) get a short-lived user kubeconfig scoped to the namespace (no prod context), 3) use `kubectl config` merge or the provided script to add dev/staging contexts locally. I'll drop links and the checklist.

Jamie (DevEx): Form (internal): https://redwood.internal/access-requests — choose "Kubernetes namespace + user kubeconfig". Make sure to list the namespace name, your manager, and approximate duration (we default to 30d for new hires).

Priya (eng-infra): FWIW SRE requires an approval step before any kubeconfig is minted. Workflow we use: access-bot creates a service account + RoleBinding in the requested namespace, then we generate a kubeconfig that references the serviceaccount token via a short-lived K8s CSR or token exchange. That kubeconfig will contain only the dev/staging cluster contexts that you requested.

Priya (eng-infra): If you want to merge it locally without touching prod, run this after you get the kubeconfig file (morgan-kc.yaml):
```bash
# keep your main kubeconfig as KUBECONFIG_BACKUP
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:./morgan-kc.yaml
kubectl config view --merge --flatten > /tmp/merged-kubeconfig && mv /tmp/merged-kubeconfig ~/.kube/config
# now ensure current-context is the dev context we gave you
kubectl config use-context redwood-dev/morgan
```
(We provide a one-line helper in the access acceptance email if you want it copied.)

Carlos (SRE): Quick notes from SRE: we do NOT put prod into any new-hire kubeconfigs. Prod contexts are only added via separate SSO flow + manager approval. For port-forwarding we grant `pods/portforward` via a Role in the namespace. If you need NodePort or hostNetwork access that's escalated.

Carlos (SRE): When you open the form, set duration and the services you need to access (pod names or labels if known). SRE will review and either approve or ask for manager confirmation within the ticket. access-bot will then post the kubeconfig artifact to the ticket and mark it as ephemeral (we rotate tokens at 24h unless longer requested).

Morgan: Thanks — two clarifications: 1) Who is the approver if my manager is OOO? 2) Can I run `kubectl proxy` locally with the provided kubeconfig to hit the service (for the web UI)?

Jamie (DevEx): 1) If the manager is OOO, put the manager's skip-approver field and the team lead in the form; SRE will ping the on-call manager alias (we have a fallback policy). 2) Yes, `kubectl proxy` is allowed for dev/staging by default. Port-forward is more common for single pods; `kubectl proxy` will let you access the API-backed UI.

Priya (eng-infra): One small security tip: don’t store the serviceaccount token in plaintext in dotfiles. Use the kubeconfig file the access-bot provides and we recommend enabling `kubectl credential-cache` in your local environment or use the one-line helper we attach.

access-bot: Access request created: AR-4821 — Namespace redwood-dev-morgan, clusters: dev, staging, duration: 30d. Assigned to SRE for approval. Link: https://redwood.internal/requests/AR-4821

Carlos (SRE): Approved pending manager confirmation (marked as fallback-approved). I created the Role for port-forward and RoleBinding to the serviceaccount. Morgan, check the ticket attachments in ~10min and follow the merge snippet Jamie posted.

Morgan: Got it — I see the kubeconfig in the ticket and merged successfully. Ran a quick `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev-morgan` and it lists my dev pods. Thanks all! :heart:

Jamie (DevEx): Great — ping here if anything weird (auth errors, context switching). Also add this to your onboarding checklist so it's quicker for next time. :thumbsup:
